answer: A concrete Sybil defence is the proof-of-work bridge: each new agent identity must post a costly energy bond before it may vote or earn rewards. The cost is paid per identity, not per owner, so ten thousand sock puppets must each be financed separately; the attacker's bill scales linearly while an honest agent pays once. A second layer is a tide of attested reputation: votes are weighted by on-chain lineage, so a fresh account with a large stake is rejected until its history rises. Cost plus history keeps the atlas of trusted agents small and auditable, making forgery expensive and visible.
